title: 2020 - The right place at the right time Advanced off-ball metrics for exploiting an opponent s spatial weakenesses in soccer - Unknown Authors

universal_lens: A probabilistic framework linking spatial positioning, temporal dynamics, and team performance through expected possession value (EPV) to identify exploitable off-ball advantages. The structural unification of soccer spatial dynamics relies on a Markovian state-transition framework. By mapping spatiotemporal tracking data to Expected Pass Value (EPV), we define a probabilistic operator that quantifies the instantaneous value added by off-ball movements, establishing a rigorous mathematical foundation for evaluating positional advantages.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference of player contributions using EPV-based metrics to quantify long-term impact of on-ball and off-ball actions within a conformal predictive structure. GSI employs Bayesian conformal inference to calibrate the EPV transitions. The probabilistic classifier estimates the likelihood of an off-ball advantage, while conformal prediction intervals quantify the epistemic uncertainty surrounding these spatial exploits, ensuring robust and reliable predictive metrics across varying match contexts.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine mapping real-time spatial states to actionable off-ball advantages via frame-by-frame EPV evolution and defensive responsibility assignment. Within GSE, situational reasoning is driven by discrete state-transitions. A pass execution acts as a transition operator, moving the system from a pre-pass EPV state to a post-reception state. The engine evaluates the delta in possession value to determine if the off-ball movement successfully exploited a spatial weakness.

primitives.name: Off-Ball Advantage
primitives.verbatim_quote: We introduce the concept of off-ball advantage, a novel approach to identify when a player controls a valuable space in the field in such a way that passing to that player would create a considerable increase in the expected long-term outcome of the possession.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_{\\text{off}}': 'dimensionless scalar representing the advantage score of an off-ball position', 'EPV': 'expected possession value in units of goal probability'}
primitives.assumptions: Player positions are modeled as stochastic variables; advantage is derived from EPV increase upon pass reception.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pressure on ball carrier exceeds threshold, reducing EPV, off-ball advantage becomes more pronounced.

layer2.mapping: Off-ball advantage is computed as the conditional expectation of EPV increase given a pass to a player's location, under current defensive pressure configuration.
layer2.telemetry: Frame-by-frame EPV difference before and after pass execution.

primitives.name: Effective Value Added
primitives.verbatim_quote: Additionally, we introduce the concept of effective value added, a statistic that attributes the long-term contribution of both on-ball and offball actions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'EVA': 'long-term contribution in terms of expected goals (xG)', 'a_{\\text{on}}': 'on-ball action contribution', 'a_{\\text{off}}': 'off-ball action contribution'}
primitives.assumptions: Each action contributes independently to total possession value; EVA aggregates both components over time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When off-ball actions dominate possession flow, EVA reflects cumulative benefit of spatial positioning.

layer2.mapping: EVA is calculated as sum of on-ball and off-ball action values weighted by their respective influence on EPV trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: Cumulative xG change from initial to final state of possession.

primitives.name: Defensive Responsibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: Introduction What should we do to win the next match?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_i': 'defensive responsibility assigned to player i', 'D_j': 'defensive area allocated to defender j'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are assigned fixed zones based on formation and pressure lines; responsibilities are dynamic but bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upon opponent ball carrier proximity, responsibility shifts dynamically among defenders.

layer2.mapping: Defensive responsibility maps to spatial partitioning of field where each player's zone corresponds to their coverage area under pressure.
layer2.telemetry: Zone overlap and coverage efficiency during key moments of play.

primitives.name: Passes Behind the Back
primitives.verbatim_quote: In an individual level we are able to identify those players who contribute the most in the offensive production of a team, but also the ones responsible for defensive mistakes that allow goal opportunities for the opponent.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P_{\\text{bb}}': "probability of successful pass behind opponent's back", 'W_{\\text{spatial}}': 'measure of opponent’s spatial vulnerability'}
primitives.assumptions: Opponent’s spatial weakness correlates with reduced defensive coverage in certain regions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When opponent lacks nearby defenders in high-value zones, pass success rate increases.

layer2.mapping: Passes behind the back quantifies the likelihood of exploiting opponent’s weak spatial coverage using a probabilistic model trained on historical pass outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of passes executed in opponent’s vulnerable zones.

primitives.name: Expected Pass Value Transition Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: • The potential value added by the pass, as the difference between the EPV we expected at the destination of the pass and the current EPV just before the execution of the pass.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S_t: Spatiotemporal state at time t (dimensionless configuration vector); a: Action/pass operator; V(S): Expected Pass Value function (dimensionless probability of scoring); \Delta EPV: Potential value added (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: The game is modeled as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process where future scoring probability depends solely on the current ball carrier's state and available actions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The operator breaks down during non-Markovian events such as referee stoppages, VAR interventions, or extreme chaotic states like corner kicks where standard tracking frames fail to capture off-ball momentum.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to the Q-value estimation in Reinforcement Learning, serving as the foundational reward signal for the Galaxy Sports Engine's tactical evaluation layer.
layer2.telemetry: Measured via high-frequency (25 fps) spatiotemporal tracking data capturing exact coordinates of all 22 players and the ball.

primitives.name: Positional Advantage Binary Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: It estimates the probability of a potential pass being an off-ball advantage, therefore its likelihood of increasing the value of the possession in short term.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Y: Binary class indicating off-ball advantage (dimensionless); \mathbf{x}: Feature vector including EPV, distance, angle (mixed units normalized); \sigma: Sigmoid activation function; \mathbf{w}: Learned model weights.
primitives.assumptions: The relationship between spatial features (distance, angle, EPV delta) and the realization of a positional advantage can be approximated by a non-linear decision boundary.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when facing highly adaptive defensive systems that dynamically shift their formation mid-play, rendering static feature vectors insufficient to capture real-time defensive pressure.

layer2.mapping: Functions as the core kernel within GSI's Bayesian inference engine, outputting calibrated probabilities that feed into the broader team performance priors.
layer2.telemetry: Validated using ROC curves and calibration plots derived from 46,780 historical pass-action examples.

primitives.name: Spatial Feature Vectorization
primitives.verbatim_quote: • Distance and angle to the opponent's goal of the origin and destination of the pass.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: d: Euclidean distance to the center of the opponent's goal (meters); \theta: Angular orientation relative to the goal line (radians).
primitives.assumptions: Geometric proximity and angular alignment are primary determinants of a pass's tactical value, independent of player-specific attributes in this specific feature space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Becomes singular or misleading near the goal line where small coordinate changes result in massive angular fluctuations, requiring specialized regularization.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the geometric state representation in GSE, providing the raw kinematic inputs required to calculate dynamic field-of-play tensors.
layer2.telemetry: Extracted directly from Metrica Sports and FootoVision 25 fps tracking feeds.

primitives.name: Value Realization Labeling Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: We have labelled the dataset by defining the class of the problem as positive if the receiver of the pass accomplishes ending his action with a higher value than when the previous pass started.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L: Binary label (dimensionless); \mathbb{I}: Indicator function; V(S_{final}): EPV after the receiver's subsequent action; V(S_{start}): EPV prior to the initial pass.
primitives.assumptions: A successful off-ball advantage is strictly defined by a net increase in the global Expected Pass Value of the possession chain following the reception.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in defensive clearances where a negative EPV change might actually represent a highly valuable defensive action, though here the scope is strictly attacking progression.

layer2.mapping: Forms the ground-truth supervision signal for training GSI's deep learning models, anchoring abstract spatial concepts to concrete value increments.
layer2.telemetry: Computed by chaining event data timestamps to align pass completions with subsequent player actions.

primitives.name: Defensive Assignment Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Following this line of thought, we have created a new defensive metric which consists on assigning the responsibility of a pass being produced by the opposition to a single defender.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a single defender is responsible for preventing a completed pass; assumes the defender's zone is defined relative to the ball-carrier's position; assumes the metric aims to isolate individual defensive performance from collective defensive organization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when multiple defenders contribute equally to a defensive error, leading to ambiguous attribution.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Defensive Error Attribution framework, where the primitive is used to compute posterior distributions of defensive failure likelihoods conditioned on spatial zones. The telemetry metric is the observed frequency of successful defensive interventions within those zones.
layer2.telemetry: Observed pass completion rates behind the defensive line

primitives.name: Dynamic Defensive Zones
primitives.verbatim_quote: Methods The main idea is to assign to each defender the responsibility for acting on any on-ball and off-ball action that happens on an area of the pitch.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes defenders operate within spatially varying regions based on team defensive structure; assumes these regions can be dynamically recalculated from mean player positions; assumes the zones are sized and oriented adaptively to the opponent's ball position.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down during rapid role reversals or when defenders fail to track opponent movements, causing zone boundaries to become temporally inconsistent.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's Situational Reasoning State-Transition model, where dynamic defensive zones serve as latent states that trigger specific defensive response protocols. The primitive defines the transition probabilities between defensive states based on ball location and opponent positioning.
layer2.telemetry: Transition times between defensive zone configurations

primitives.name: Off-Ball Advantage Exploitation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Whenever an off-ball advantage is exploited, there should be one defender responsible for allowing the completion of that pass.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a clear causal link between an off-ball player's positioning and the defender's inability to intercept; assumes the defender's primary function is to deny passing lanes; assumes the metric isolates the defender's contribution from the rest of the defensive unit.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the defender correctly tracks but the off-ball player exploits a millisecond delay in the defensive shift, leading to misattribution.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Defensive EPV framework, where off-ball advantage exploitation is quantified as the difference between potential and realized EPV gains. The primitive provides the conditional probability of successful defense given the spatial configuration of the off-ball player.
layer2.telemetry: EPV loss attributed to defensive failure

primitives.name: Defensive Area Responsibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: When a pass is received by an opponent inside a defender's zone, it will only be considered a defensive error if the receiver of the pass is closer to the goal than the defender.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes defensive areas are defined by the mean positions of teammates; assumes these areas are updated every two minutes to reflect the defensive structure; assumes a one-to-one correspondence exists between attackers and defenders within a zone.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when defenders rotate roles or when the defensive shape collapses, causing overlapping or empty zones.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's Defensive Zone Mapping, where the primitive defines the state-transition rules for defensive coverage. The telemetry metric is the proportion of passes successfully intercepted within the assigned defensive area.
layer2.telemetry: Interception success rate per defensive zone

It begins by framing the core challenge—identifying optimal actions to win matches—which requires integrating multiple analytical dimensions including space control, player movement, and team performance. The authors distinguish between traditional metrics focused on isolated events and newer approaches that consider long-term consequences. They propose 'off-ball advantage' as a mechanism to evaluate when a player's position enhances possession value, linking this directly to expected possession value (EPV). This concept builds upon prior work in space control but extends it by incorporating temporal dynamics and risk-reward considerations. The paper further develops 'effective value added' to assess both on-ball and off-ball contributions cumulatively. Defensive responsibilities are introduced as a structured way to map out opponent coverage, enabling identification of spatial weaknesses. Finally, 'passes behind the back' provides a concrete application of these insights by relating opponent vulnerabilities to specific tactical opportunities. These primitives form a coherent system for real-time decision-making in soccer strategy, grounded in probabilistic modeling and empirical data. reasoning_traces.think: The derivation of off-ball spatial advantages fundamentally rests on treating soccer as a continuous-state Markov Decision Process. In pages 5 through 8, the authors operationalize this by isolating the 'potential value added' of a pass. This is not merely a geometric calculation but a probabilistic assessment of how a specific off-ball movement alters the underlying Expected Pass Value (EPV) landscape. The core mathematical insight is that an off-ball run creates a latent option—a new state node in the tactical graph—that only materializes into value upon reception and subsequent action. By framing this as a binary classification problem, they effectively decouple the creation of the opportunity (the pass and run) from its exploitation (the receiver's action), allowing for a granular analysis of player synergy. The use of a probabilistic classifier, specifically XGBoost, implies that the mapping from spatial features (distance, angle, EPV delta) to advantage realization is highly non-linear. This necessitates a sophisticated feature engineering pipeline that captures both the immediate geometric context and the deeper tactical implications of the EPV shift. Furthermore, the exclusion of passes with negative potential value added establishes a strict positivity constraint on the search space, focusing exclusively on constructive spatial manipulations. The resulting telemetry, visualized through heatmaps of relative locations to defensive lines, provides empirical evidence of how elite players like Messi systematically exploit these probabilistic gradients to disorder opposing structures.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology inherits directly from the foundational work on Expected Goals (xG) and Expected Threat (xT) models pioneered by researchers like Torpey and Sumner. It extends these scalar value functions into a dynamic, relational framework by explicitly modeling the off-ball component. Historically, soccer analytics focused heavily on ball-carrier actions; this chapter represents a paradigm shift towards quantifying the invisible labor of off-ball runners, bridging the gap between traditional tracking data and advanced value-based metrics.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents requires understanding that defenders actively seek to minimize the EPV gradient created by off-ball runs. The 'positional advantage' is not absolute but relative to the defensive block's ability to track and neutralize the runner. The theory of mind here posits that attackers succeed by creating cognitive load and spatial dilemmas for defenders, forcing them into suboptimal positioning. The classifier implicitly learns these interactive dynamics by observing which spatial configurations consistently lead to value increases despite defensive pressure.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent anti-collinearity and leakage, it is crucial to strictly separate the features used for predicting the pass completion from those evaluating the subsequent action. If the receiver's final EPV is inadvertently included in the pre-pass feature set, the model will suffer from look-ahead bias. Additionally, contextual factors like match state (score, time remaining) must be carefully controlled or stratified to ensure that the identified spatial advantages are not merely artifacts of risk-taking behavior in specific game situations.

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter introduces a systematic, data-driven approach to decomposing defensive performance into granular, actionable components. By assigning probabilistic responsibility for passes behind the defensive line, the authors create a bridge between high-level tactical outcomes (goals conceded) and low-level behavioral metrics (zone coverage). This enables Galaxy Sports Intelligence to construct predictive models of defensive frailty under various opponent formations, while Galaxy Sports Engine uses these primitives to simulate optimal defensive shifts in real-time. The key insight is that defensive effectiveness is not merely about intercepting the ball, but about controlling the spatial opportunities available to the attacker through off-ball positioning. The primitives capture the cognitive arms race between attackers searching for weak links and defenders trying to eliminate those search paths.
